I found two non-test callers, one in each of the `loaddata` and `dumpdata` management commands:

```json
{"callers": ["django/core/management/commands/loaddata.py::Command.handle", "django/core/management/commands/dumpdata.py::Command.handle"]}
```

I searched only the `django/` package, so callers outside it (for example in docs or scripts) weren't checked. Inside the package, `add_to_class` is called directly from three places:

```json
{"callers": ["django/db/models/base.py::ModelBase.__new__", "django/db/models/base.py::ModelBase._prepare", "django/db/models/options.py::Options._prepare"]}
```

I found four direct non-test callers, all in Django's management commands. Three are inside `handle`; the squash one is inside a helper method called `find_migration`.

```json
{"callers": ["django/core/management/commands/squashmigrations.py::Command.find_migration", "django/core/management/commands/sqlmigrate.py::Command.handle", "django/core/management/commands/optimizemigration.py::Command.handle", "django/core/management/commands/migrate.py::Command.handle"]}
```

I found three direct non-test callers. This comes from a text search for `clean_ipv6_address` outside `tests/` and checking which function each call sits in. Two calls are in `GenericIPAddressField` in `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py`. The third is in `GenericIPAddressField.to_python` in `django/forms/fields.py`.

```json
{"callers": ["django/db/models/fields/__init__.py::GenericIPAddressField.to_python", "django/db/models/fields/__init__.py::GenericIPAddressField.get_prep_value", "django/forms/fields.py::GenericIPAddressField.to_python"]}
```
